{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Tatsu is a steel flying roller coaster designed by Bolliger & Mabillard at the Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park located in Valencia, California, United States.","title":"Tatsu"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Announced on November 17, 2005, the roller coaster opened to the public on May 13, 2006 as the park's seventeenth roller coaster.","title":"Tatsu"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Tatsu reaches a height of 170 ft and speeds up to 62 mph .","title":"Tatsu"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The ride's name means \"Flying Beast\" in Japanese.","title":"Tatsu"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" The roller coaster is also the world's tallest and fastest flying coaster; is the only flying roller coaster to feature a zero-gravity roll; and has the world's highest pretzel loop.","title":"Tatsu"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" It was the world's longest flying coaster until The Flying Dinosaur surpassed it.","title":"Tatsu"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Skyscraper is an upcoming roller coaster that will be located at the planned Skyplex complex in Orlando, Florida.","title":"Skyscraper (roller coaster)"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Under development by American and Swiss manufacturers US Thrill Rides and Intamin, the attraction will be a Polercoaster model which utilizes an observation tower as its main support structure.","title":"Skyscraper (roller coaster)"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" After several delays, Skyscraper is expected to open in 2020 with construction on the Skyplex complex beginning in 2017.","title":"Skyscraper (roller coaster)"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Upon completion, it will become the tallest roller coaster in the world at over 500 ft and will feature both the steepest drop and highest inversion.","title":"Skyscraper (roller coaster)"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"Skyplex has which roller coaster that will become the tallest in the world when it opens in 2020?"}
